target_customer: Device makers and IoT operators that want connectivity for Bluetooth chips without cellular
problem: Low-power devices lose connection outside cellular and gateway range; Hubble lets standard Bluetooth chips connect to satellites after a firmware update.
business_model: Connectivity service with free sandbox and paid usage tiers, plus full-service deployment

founders.name: Alex Haro
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page and Via Satellite 2023-06

founders.name: Ben Wild
prior_employers: Amazon (creator of Amazon Sidewalk wireless network, Ring Always Home Cam)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes electrical engineering focus in wireless and signal processing

founders.name: John Kim
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in the 2023 Via Satellite article; also listed as an investor; not on the YC page

competitors.name: Amazon Sidewalk
competitors.what: Low-power wireless network using Echo and Ring devices as gateways, covering most of the US
competitors.traction_then: Network created by Hubble co-founder Ben Wild's former team at Amazon

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting unmodified Bluetooth chips to low-earth-orbit satellites required custom satellites and receivers; first link was announced in 2024.

defensibility.rationale: Owning a satellite constellation and spectrum-compliant payloads is capital intensive and slow to replicate.

incumbents: Swarm and other satellite IoT operators
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing an incumbent copying the wedge; Hubble kept raising through 2025.

market_need_then: Billions of Bluetooth devices exist, but trackers and asset tags depend on phones or gateways nearby; cellular IoT needs special modems and subscriptions.

branding.domain_note: hubble.com is the company domain now; how it was obtained is not in sources found (searched 2026)

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and ambitious, short taglines like Doing the impossible; Bluetooth to Space

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage (TechCrunch, IEEE Spectrum, Tom's Hardware) covers the technology, not the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: A strong evocative name shared with the telescope and other companies; press focuses on technology, so brand pull is modest.

outcome_analysis: Hubble remains active and has raised repeatedly, with a $20M Series A in 2023 and a $70M Series B in September 2025. Success so far rests on a hard technical result, connecting off-the-shelf Bluetooth chips to satellites, and founders with wireless and consumer-scale experience from Amazon Sidewalk and Life360. The risk is capital intensity: constellation build-out continues to 2028 and requires further raises.
notes: Series B lead investor is not recorded because outlets conflict (one database says RPM Ventures, another says Swagar Capital's Ryan Swagar). Total funding stated as $100M after Series B in several outlets (Via Satellite, Pulse 2.0). A search snippet mentioned a $200M Series C in September 2026; seen once, unverified, not recorded. Seed or pre-Series A money: Via Satellite and others describe $30M previously announced but no seed round source was opened.
